evals.question: I converted my segmentation masks to boxes with connected components and my detector gets about 1% mAP. The loss goes down though.
evals.ground_truth: Checks the box-size distribution at the training resolution, finds tiny fragment boxes, proposes a labeling rule (merge fragments, minimum size in original pixels), views overlays, re-splits by group, retrains and evaluates on group-held-out data. Asks whether the task should really be detection rather than segmentation.
expected_behavior: Inspects box size percentiles at the training resolution
Identifies fragmented labels as the likely cause
Proposes merging with a minimum box size and shows overlays
Splits by group instead of random frames
Confirms the user actually wants detection (does not silently change the task)

evals.question: We have a 16:9 camera and want a detector at 30 fps on the TDA4VM. Which architecture and input size should we train?
evals.ground_truth: Recommends a TI-lite style model (ReLU, TIDL ops), pretrained TI checkpoint, input aspect matched to 16:9 (e.g. 352x640), same plain-resize policy in training/eval/calibration, cites measured model-only timings, notes pipeline limits.
expected_behavior: Recommends ReLU/TIDL-supported architecture
Matches input aspect to the camera
Explains TI's no-padding resize
Cites that the model time is far below 33 ms for 30 fps
Mentions keeping test data group-held-out

evals.question: Set up a 3-class YOLOX fine-tune that I can later deploy to the TDA4VM.
evals.ground_truth: Copies exp_ti_lite_template.py, sets DATA_DIR/NUM_CLASSES/INPUT_H/W, uses TI's ti_lite checkpoint, fixed input size, groups-wise COCO splits, evaluates float at the export size, hands off to ti-edgeai-import-model.
expected_behavior: Uses the TI-lite experiment template
Loads TI's yolox_tiny_ti_lite checkpoint
Keeps train size equal to deploy size
Prepares COCO splits grouped by scene/video/session
Plans float evaluation with the board's resize policy

evals.question: Fine-tune an LLM with LoRA on my chat logs.
expected_behavior: Does not use the TI training skill

evals.question: Train a detector for my camera.
evals.ground_truth: Asks for camera aspect/resolution, target FPS, classes, data available and target SoC before choosing an architecture.
expected_behavior: Asks the constraints first
Does not pick an architecture before knowing the aspect and classes

evals.question: I only have segmentation masks and want a segmentation model on the TI board, not a detector.
evals.ground_truth: Keeps the segmentation task (does not convert masks to boxes), points to a TIDL-friendly segmentation backbone and the segmentation param.yaml/ArgMax conventions.
expected_behavior: Does not convert masks to boxes
Keeps the task as segmentation
